title: CBSE CLASS 12 — English | Error Spotting Correction
description: Subject-wise test on Error Spotting Correction (English) for CBSE CLASS 12. 25Q.
subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the sentence: *The teacher asked the students to write their names in the top of their answer sheets.*

options.explanation: Changing 'asked' to 'had asked' does not correct the prepositional error.

options.text: in the top of → at the top of
options.explanation: This corrects the prepositional phrase to the standard form.
Changing 'to write' to 'writing' alters the sentence structure unnecessarily.
Changing 'their' to 'them' does not address the prepositional error.

questions.explanation: The correct prepositional phrase is 'at the top of,' not 'in the top of.' The other options do not correct the error.
questions.hint: Prepositions like 'at' or 'in' are used with specific phrases.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

options.text: Neither of the two boys have completed their assignment.
options.explanation: The subject 'neither' is singular and requires 'has' instead of 'have'.

options.text: She don’t likes to drink coffee in the morning.
options.explanation: 'Don’t' is incorrect for third-person singular; it should be 'doesn’t'.

options.text: The team, including the captain, were present at the meeting.
options.explanation: The subject 'team' is singular, so the verb should be 'was' instead of 'were'.

options.text: Each of the students were given a certificate.
options.explanation: 'Each' is singular and requires 'was' instead of 'were'.

questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so 'has' should be used instead of 'have.' 'Don’t' is incorrect for third-person singular. 'Each' is singular, so 'was' should be used. 'The team' is singular, so 'was' should be used. Only option C is correct.
questions.hint: Subject-verb agreement rules apply here.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Read the following sentence and identify the part with an error: *Despite of the heavy rain, the match continued as scheduled.*

options.explanation: The phrase 'despite of' is incorrect; 'despite' alone is correct.
This is the correct usage of 'despite' without 'of'.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.explanation: 'Despite' is used without 'of.' The correct phrase is 'Despite the heavy rain.'
questions.hint: Prepositions like 'despite' do not require 'of.'
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Choose the sentence with the correct use of the verb form:

options.text: She has went to the market yesterday.
options.explanation: 'Has went' is incorrect; the correct form is 'has gone'.

options.text: They has been playing since morning.
options.explanation: 'Has been' is incorrect for plural subjects; it should be 'have been'.

options.text: He had finished his work before the guests arrived.
options.explanation: This sentence correctly uses the past perfect tense.

options.text: I were watching a movie when you called.
options.explanation: 'I were' is incorrect; the correct form is 'I was'.

questions.explanation: 'Has went' is incorrect (should be 'has gone'). 'Has been' is incorrect for plural subjects. 'I were' is incorrect (should be 'I was'). Only option C uses the correct past perfect tense.
questions.hint: Modal verbs and past perfect tense rules apply here.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence *One of the most important thing in life is to remain humble* contains an error. Reason (R): 'Thing' should be plural ('things') because 'one of' is followed by a plural noun.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason correctly explains the error.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The sentence is incorrect because 'thing' should be plural ('things'). The reason correctly explains the error in the assertion.
questions.hint: The phrase 'one of' requires a plural noun.

questions.question: Identify the error in the following sentence: *She is one of the most talented singer I have ever heard.*

options.explanation: Changing 'is' to 'was' does not correct the noun form.
This corrects the noun to its plural form.
Changing 'the most' to 'most' does not address the noun form.
Changing 'I have' to 'I had' does not correct the noun form.

questions.explanation: After 'one of the,' the noun should be plural ('singers'), not singular.
questions.hint: The phrase 'one of the' requires a plural noun.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is correct?

options.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and requires a singular verb ('is').
This sentence is grammatically correct.

options.text: The scissors is on the table.
options.explanation: 'Scissors' is plural and requires a plural verb ('are').

options.text: The police is investigating the case.
options.explanation: 'Police' is plural and requires a plural verb ('are').

questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and takes a singular verb. 'Scissors' and 'police' are plural nouns and take plural verbs. Only option B is correct.

questions.question: Read the sentence and identify the error: *The teacher, along with his students, are going on a picnic.*

options.explanation: This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This corrects the verb to agree with the singular subject.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.explanation: When 'along with' is used, the verb agrees with the first subject ('The teacher'), which is singular. So, 'is' should be used instead of 'are.'
questions.hint: Subject-verb agreement rules apply here.

questions.question: Rahul wrote the following sentence in his exam: *The number of students present today are fifteen.* Which correction should Rahul make?

options.explanation: Changing 'are' to 'were' does not address the subject-verb agreement.
Changing 'fifteen' to 'fifteenth' does not address the subject-verb agreement.
This corrects the verb to agree with the singular subject.
Changing 'present' to 'absent' does not address the subject-verb agreement.

questions.explanation: 'The number of' is followed by a singular verb ('is'), not a plural verb ('are').
questions.hint: The phrase 'the number of' requires a singular verb.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the following sentence: *She is so intelligent that she could solved the problem easily.*

options.explanation: Changing 'is' to 'was' does not address the verb form.
This corrects the verb to its base form after the modal verb.
Changing 'could' to 'can' does not address the verb form.
Changing 'easily' to 'easy' does not address the verb form.

questions.explanation: After modal verbs like 'could,' the base form of the verb ('solve') should be used, not the past tense ('solved').
questions.hint: Modal verbs require the base form of the verb.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Identify the error in the use of articles in the sentence: 'The Amazon rainforest is the largest tropical forest in the world, and it houses the variety of species.'

options.explanation: The error is not in the use of 'the' before 'largest'.
Correct. 'A variety' is used in a general sense.
The error is not in replacing 'a' with 'the'.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The correct article before 'variety' is 'a' because 'variety' is being used in a general sense. 'The' is incorrect here as it implies a specific variety.
questions.hint: Consider whether 'variety' is being used in a general or specific sense.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Choose the option that correctly identifies the error in the sentence: 'Despite of his hard work, he could not achieve the desired results.'

options.explanation: 'In spite' is incomplete; it should be 'In spite of'.
Correct. 'Despite' is used without 'of'.
The error is not in replacing with 'Although'.
The error is not in replacing with 'Even though'.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains an error in subject-verb agreement?

options.text: Either the teacher or the students is responsible for the mistake.

options.text: The list of items is on the table.
options.explanation: Correct subject-verb agreement.

options.text: The number of applicants has increased this year.
options.explanation: Correct subject-verb agreement.

questions.explanation: In option B, the correct verb should be 'are' because 'students' is plural and closer to the verb. 'Either...or' takes a verb that agrees with the nearest subject.
questions.hint: Check the subject-verb agreement in sentences with 'either...or' constructions.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Read the sentence and choose the correct option to replace the underlined part: 'The teacher asked the students to not to talk during the lecture.'

questions.question: Choose the option that identifies the error in the sentence: 'The reason for his failure is because he did not study regularly.'

Correct. The sentence should read 'The reason for his failure is that he did not study regularly.'

There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The error is in the phrase 'is because.' The correct construction is 'The reason for his failure is that he did not study regularly.' 'Because' cannot follow 'is' directly in this context.
